key_insight: Latent image tokens live on thin spherical shells and their semantic/perceptual content is carried mostly by direction; aligning and matching latent geometry on the sphere (rather than along Euclidean chords) yields more faithful generative transport.
problem_solved: Standard latent flow matching moves Gaussian noise to VAE latents along straight Euclidean chords, which exit the thin spherical shells that endpoints occupy and harm semantic fidelity and generative quality.
method: Decompose each latent token into radial and angular components and analyze contribution via component‑swap probes to show direction dominates semantics.
Perform flow matching on the angular (directional) part using spherical/geodesic-aware transports while treating radius separately (e.g., preserve or model radial distribution).
Preprocess or align radii and enforce spherical geometry during training so flows remain on-shell and better preserve decoded content.
impact: By respecting spherical latent geometry, the approach reduces off‑shell transport that distorts semantics, improving generation fidelity, robustness, and efficiency for latent-space generative models.
visual_elements: Diagram of latent clouds: two thin spherical shells with an Euclidean chord leaving the shells vs. a spherical/geodesic path staying on the shell
Illustration of latent decomposition into radius + direction with arrows showing semantic content aligned with direction
Component-swap examples: decoded images when swapping angles vs. radii to show direction carries semantics
Chart comparing generation quality or reconstruction metrics for Euclidean vs. spherical flow matching
paper_title: Aligning Latent Geometry for Spherical Flow Matching in Image Generation
paper_authors: Tuna Han Salih Meral, Kaan Oktay, Hidir Yesiltepe, Adil Kaan Akan, Pinar Yanardag
